The number of ranks a character has in a list determines the level to which he can cast from that list (e.g., if a character has 8 ranks in Fire Law he can cast any spell from the Fire Law list up to 8th level). The number of ranks in the spell list plus the caster’s realm stat bonus (once) is also added to the Spellcasting Roll when a spell is cast. The full skill bonus in a Spell List is used for Spell Mastery: attempts to change the spell when it is cast (e.g., making a Fire Ball diameter smaller or shaping a Wall of Fire). Other uses are occasionally specified in certain spells.

There are 5 different Spell List skills: Base, Open, Closed, Arcane, and Restricted, with each individual spell list as specializations. Base lists are the specialized spell lists of each magic-using profession. Open lists are common, relatively straightforward spells that may be understood by anyone using the realm. Closed lists represent more esoteric magical techniques which may be understood by any user of the realm, but with greater difficulty. Arcane lists are more obscure or exotic magics which exist outside of the three realms. Restricted lists include any list the GM allows you to learn which is not a Base, Open, Closed, or Arcane list (e.g., the Base list of another profession). You may not develop ranks in lists from realms other than your own.

Each Base, Open, Closed, Arcane, or Restricted Spell List requires separate skill specialization

system.name: Concealment
system.description:
Concealment is the skill to hide items or groups of items of any size (e.g., building,
campsite), or even people using the environment, taking advantage of lighting, and using
camouflage where appropriate. For an individual character trying to remain unseen either
moving or stationary, use the Stalking skill.

system.name: Footwork
system.description: Reduces penalties associated with movement while making melee attacks (including charging) (Section 8.2).

system.name: Region Lore
system.description:
This skill provides knowledge about the geography of a region, as well as a basic overview
of local cultures, flora, fauna, and a limited history. The region size may vary but
should be no more than 100,000 square miles (about 300 x 300 miles, roughly the size of
the state of Colorado or the nation of Italy).

system.name: Protect
system.description: Reduces penalties for extending your DB to protect an ally (Section 9.7).

system.name: Medicine
system.description:
This skill provides a bonus for treating injuries and overt symptoms of illness. This
skill includes the use of simple medical aids/herbs, setting broken bones, stopping
bleeding, etc. For detailed use of this skill see the rules on injuries and healing
(Section 13.1).

system.name: Writing
system.description:
The written word holds civilization together.
With written records, knowledge can be transmitted great distances and preserved over time
on scales that far surpass what is possible with an oral tradition.
Written compositions may be used to inform, to teach, to inspire, or to entertain. A
skilled writer may imply rather than needing to state outright, encouraging a reader to
draw the right conclusions, or they may sow confusion and doubt. If the objective is to
persuade the reader, Writing may be used in place of the Influence skill.

system.name: Control Lycanthropy
system.description:
The infectious shape changing inflicted by lycanthropy is provoked by instinct and emotion
and controlled through discipline and calm. The emotional urge to give in to the inner
animal rises and falls with the lunar cycle, being hardest to resist at the full moon.
Each time the character goes to sleep on a full moon, any time the player (or GM) has the
character displaying real rage, and any time the GM feels the character is being put under
extreme emotional stress, an Absolute Maneuver should be rolled against this skill (at -25
if 0 ranks) to see if the character transforms into his bestial form. If this happens, the
lycanthrope (under the control of the GM) will hunt, kill and feed, violently attacking
anyone who interferes. Once its hunger is sated, it will find a place to hide and sleep.
During this sleep, it will transform back into “human” form and awaken back in control of
himself with no memory of the transformation or what he did while in bestial form.
A lycanthrope can attempt to change into bestial form while maintaining control at an
additional -25 to the maneuver, and transform from controlled beast to “human” form at an
additional -50 to the maneuver.
Failure at either type of change will result in the lycanthrope slipping into uncontrolled
state per the paragraph above.
Physical stress and trauma (injury and fatigue penalties) make it harder to control
lycanthropy and should be applied as penalties to the maneuver; it is up to the GM to
assess any mental or emotional stresses that may be worthy of penalties as well.
Meditation, sedative herbs or drugs, or magical effects that give bonuses to calm or
self-discipline can all give bonuses to control checks of this skill.

system.name: Meditation
system.description:
Meditation can be used to enter and exploit a mental trance which the character can use to
help solve difficult problems or perform mental maneuvers.
To use this skill, the character must meditate for 5 minutes. With a successful maneuver
the character gets a +25 the following round to all mental actions (attuning to a magical
item, casting a spell, using a lore skill, etc.).

system.name: Attunement
system.description:
Some items require attunement prior to using some or all of their abilities (as opposed to
a magical sword with a +10 OB, where you would normally get the bonus even if you were
unaware of it). Attunement may also be used as a method of identifying items with respect
to magical powers. The attunement process involves the formation of a sympathetic bond
between the auras of the attuning individual and item.
Normally, only one individual can be attuned to an item at a time, though an individual
may be attuned to any number of items.
The process of attunement normally requires three minutes to attempt. If the Attunement
maneuver is attempted more quickly, it is done at a penalty. For one minute, the penalty
is -10. For half a minute, the penalty is -25. Attempting to attune to an item in a single
round is -50. In any case, attunement must occur before the round in which an item is to
be used.
While the process of attunement must be done by the character who will be using the item
(if the attunement is to allow use, rather than for identification), a character may aid
another character with Attunement by explaining the power(s) and also through the use of
the Complementary Skill rule (adding his own ranks in Attunement), although only one such
person is allowed to aid the person attempting the attunement.
Once the character is attuned to an item, spell abilities may be used, making a modified
Spell-casting Roll (SCR), as described in Spell Law. Attunement and the use of magical
items is covered in more detail in Treasure Law.

system.name: Written
system.description:
The ability to communicate with or to understand any language is determined by the
language skill. This skill must be specialized as written, spoken, or signaled versions of
a language. Non-spoken communications including codes, sign language, flag signals, or the
like are considered languages for skill purposes.
Table 3-13c indicates the fluency in spoken and written languages given the ranks. Most
language skills are considered proficient with 4-6 ranks, although some simple languages
or codes may only require a few ranks to master (Morse code). Ranks beyond 10 delve into
the variations of a language over time or by region. Scholars of languages would be able
to recognize or recite important speeches or famous written works.
Example: A person with 10 ranks of English and a +50 skill bonus would have knowledge of
regional dialects of English from across the globe, but additional ranks may be helpful in
understanding something as old as Chaucer.
In some situations, even when a character has basic fluency in a language, stress or
rushing may lead to confusion (tense diplomacy, fast talking, strong accents, dialects,
etc.). The skill bonus may be used to determine if communication is successful, by
treating it as a Percentage Maneuver and a difficulty based on the situation. The GM can
garble the words to reflect the percentage of success. Each new phrase should be treated
the same way, but if someone keeps repeating the same exact words, further PM rolls will
add up as normal.
Example: The angry Sindonese customs official pushes his way through the 10 soldiers
pointing crossbows at Captain Rolf, and quickly and angrily demands “Do you have
permission to dock at the imperial wharf?!?” The GM has Captain Rolf make a PM in his
Sindonese Language skill at Hard, as the official is shouting, moving his head a lot and
talking quickly, making it hard to understand. The result is 60%, so considering, the GM
tells Captain Rolf “The angry man in the uniform shouts at you while waving his finger all
around at you, the ship and the dock, you think he said ‘Do you have letters to deliver at
the Dragon’s harbor?!?”. Captain Rolf has no idea what the official means and asks
“What…?” Hopefully the official repeats himself.

system.name: Restricted Quarters
system.description: Reduces penalties when fighting in restricted quarters (Section 9.5).

system.name: Maneuvering in Armor
system.description:
Reduces the maneuver penalty for armor worn, but has no effect on the encumbrance penalty
for armor worn (Section 7.2).

system.name: Materials Lore
system.description:
Knowledge of a specific type of material such as metal includes identification of the raw
material, as well as knowledge of sources and methods of working (crafting uses the
separate Crafting skill). Materials Lore may also include information on famous magical,
historic, legendary or cursed types of materials and items made from those materials.

system.name: Leathercraft
system.description:
Animal hide may be cured and used for all kinds of purposes. It is tough and weather proof
and it looks nice. Many items are made from leather.

system.name: Drawing/Painting
system.description:
Drawing and painting are used to create visual
art ranging from realistic representations to vague
abstraction. The artist uses lines, shading, shapes, color
and texture to create illustrations or pictures. Fine
work may require a pencil, pen, paintbrush, or similar
tool, but this skill can be crudely performed with any
usable surface and nothing else but a pigment of some
sort and the character’s finger.

system.name: Multiple Attacks
system.description:
Reduces penalties associated with making simultaneous melee attacks in a single round,
either against a single foe or multiple opponents (see Katas in Section 9.7).

system.name: Ambush
system.description:
Ambush is the ability to make a very precise attack and can only occur when the opponent
is completely unaware of the character’s attack. In such a situation, the ambushing
character makes an attack roll as normal (with a bonus for surprise and frequently for a
rear or flank attack). If a critical is obtained, the character may modify his roll on the
appropriate Critical Strike Table. The roll can be adjusted up or down by any number up to
the character’s ranks in the Ambush skill. A separate Ambush maneuver is not required.
Ambush may be used against a foe already in a melee situation if the foe is unaware of the
attack, but because position is relatively unpredictable in a general melee situation,
Ambush skill rank is halved in this case.
If the target is killed or knocked unconscious from the attack, the Ambush skill can also
be used to make the attack silent. An Absolute Maneuver roll is made and if successful
then the attack and target do not make any noise (unless the GM determines the type of
attack cannot be made silently). The difficulty of the maneuver should be based on how
loud the attack made is, and how close any observers are.
Specializations are on combat training specializations or directed spell specializations.

system.name: Subduing
system.description: Reduces penalties when trying to subdue an opponent (Section 9.7).

system.name: Adrenal Defense
system.description:
Adrenal Defense is the complete integration of dodging into fluid natural movements. With
a successful maneuver the character may perform partial dodging as an instantaneous action
(0 AP), or full dodging with concentration. Adrenal Defense is easier to maintain than
other adrenal maneuvers, so the duration is doubled. On an Absolute Success, double
benefits indicates the character may perform full dodging as an instantaneous action
during the first round. An Absolute Failure means the character is unable to dodge at all
the following round (in addition to the table result).

system.name: Climbing
system.description:
Climbing includes maneuvers from climbing a ladder to scaling a cliff. Climbing speed is
1/4 of the character’s normal Base Movement Rate (BMR).
This base rate is adjusted by pace as normal. However, climbing faster than a ‘Jog’ (x2)
is not allowed unless there are plenty of obvious hand and footholds (such as a ladder or
tree), or if the character has claws or is otherwise physically specialized for climbing
movement.

system.name: Trading
system.description:
Trading is used to negotiate, haggle, and strike bargains. Characters who are good at this
skill will be able to figure out a deal that works for both parties, if a deal is
possible. In some cases this may be resolved as an opposed Absolute Maneuver. For
haggling, resolve as an opposed Percentage Maneuver with the buyer as the active party.
The final price is 200% - result, giving a price from 50% to 200%.
The difficulty is based on how the deal the player is offering would look to the target.
If the deal seems safe and very favorable for the target it should be easy to convince
him, while if the deal seems to shortchange the target or put him in trouble or danger it
will be more difficult, or perhaps impossible.

system.name: Poison Mastery
system.description:
Poison Mastery includes knowledge of effects and doses, preparation and application of
health-destroying chemicals or diseases. This skill also covers the preparation and
application of antidotes to those toxins.

system.name: Service
system.description:
Vocations that primarily deal with interaction and providing services to others are part
of the Service skill. Interacting with customers and clients is a critical part of these
vocations, and those with the skill know how to present and conduct themselves in the
course of business as well as how to find clients.
Many service vocations will require other skills (e.g., an Innkeeper may know Trading or
Culinary, a Guide will need Region Lore, a Researcher will need Lore or Science skills).
Such skills will often be usable as Complementary skills, e.g. Bodyguard may be used as
Complementary to Perception while protecting a client.

system.name: Stage Magic
system.description:
Stage magic is the act of performing carefully choreographed tricks, usually using props.
This includes small-scale magic such as card tricks and large-scale tricks such as
‘cutting’ a person in half.

system.name: Trickery
system.description:
Practitioners of this skill have trained their hands in the art of misdirection to perform
acts that may almost seem magical to the untrained eye, but are not.
Trickery includes any sleight of hand such as might be used in cheating at cards or other
games of chance, or picking pockets.

system.name: Riding
system.description:
Riding includes the ability to stay on the mount safely as well as controlling the mount.
Characters who lack any riding skill will struggle just to remain seated on an animal when
it is moving (an unskilled rider can perform no actions other than perception and
conversation while his mount is in motion). The animal will need to be led by someone
else, or it will go where it pleases, as the unskilled rider has no control.
Horses are herd animals, however, and if a mounted group is in motion, a horse not being
led with an unskilled rider will follow the “herd” until spooked or threatened, at which
point it will flee (following the group if they all flee, or in the direction away from
what scared it if not). If the mount moves at faster than a walk, an unskilled rider will need 
to at least partially succeed on a riding maneuver (at the usual -25 penalty for 0 ranks) 
every round to avoid being thrown. For complex riding maneuvers or controlling the mount in 
stressful situations, a riding maneuver is required, with a modifier of half the movement penalty 
as shown in Table 5-3 in Chapter 5. All other Maneuvers and actions (like spell casting or attacks)
made while riding are subject to the full penalty due to the pace of the mount (Table 5-3), which may
be reduced with the Mounted Combat skill. All maneuvers that require the mount to back up
are at an additional -20.

system.name: Leadership
system.description:
Leadership is used to inspire those loyal to you to follow your instructions or to
effectively organize a group. This skill cannot be used on those not already loyal to you,
but for those who view you as their leader, this skill can be used to rally or inspire
them. Any instruction or command given that might be resisted or questioned (i.e., one
that requires a morale check; see Section 14.3) is modified by your Leadership bonus.
Also, all combatants who consider you their leader get a bonus equal to your ranks in
leadership to any RRs vs. Fear/Terror as long as they are aware that you are present. The
leader may also make a maneuver to rally followers affected by a failed fear check
(Section 14.3).
Leadership also provides a benefit when coordinating multiple individuals in a task. See
Complementary Skills at the beginning of this chapter for details.

system.name: Lip Reading
system.description:
The ability to communicate with or to understand any language is determined by the
language skill. This skill must be specialized as written, spoken, or signaled versions of
a language. Non-spoken communications including codes, sign language, flag signals, or the
like are considered languages for skill purposes.
Table 3-13c indicates the fluency in spoken and written languages given the ranks. Most
language skills are considered proficient with 4-6 ranks, although some simple languages
or codes may only require a few ranks to master (Morse code). Ranks beyond 10 delve into
the variations of a language over time or by region. Scholars of languages would be able
to recognize or recite important speeches or famous written works.
Example: A person with 10 ranks of English and a +50 skill bonus would have knowledge of
regional dialects of English from across the globe, but additional ranks may be helpful in
understanding something as old as Chaucer.
In some situations, even when a character has basic fluency in a language, stress or
rushing may lead to confusion (tense diplomacy, fast talking, strong accents, dialects,
etc.). The skill bonus may be used to determine if communication is successful, by
treating it as a Percentage Maneuver and a difficulty based on the situation. The GM can
garble the words to reflect the percentage of success. Each new phrase should be treated
the same way, but if someone keeps repeating the same exact words, further PM rolls will
add up as normal.
Example: The angry Sindonese customs official pushes his way through the 10 soldiers
pointing crossbows at Captain Rolf, and quickly and angrily demands “Do you have
permission to dock at the imperial wharf?!?” The GM has Captain Rolf make a PM in his
Sindonese Language skill at Hard, as the official is shouting, moving his head a lot and
talking quickly, making it hard to understand. The result is 60%, so considering, the GM
tells Captain Rolf “The angry man in the uniform shouts at you while waving his finger all
around at you, the ship and the dock, you think he said ‘Do you have letters to deliver at
the Dragon’s harbor?!?”. Captain Rolf has no idea what the official means and asks
“What…?” Hopefully the official repeats himself.

system.name: Metalcraft
system.description:
Metals are unearthed and the ore melted down and refined into ingots or billets. Each
metal has its own uses and many specializations exist to make metal objects. It can be
molded or worked. Sample metals include the hard and tough iron, the semi-precious and
malleable copper, precious but soft silver and gold and others.

system.name: Power Development
system.description:
The total bonus for this skill determines the number of Power Points that a character will
have available for spell casting. Each character has a single pool of Power Points (PP),
even if that character has access to multiple realms.
Power Points are recovered through rest. For each 2 hours of sleep the character will
regain 10% of their Power Point total, for up to a full night of sleep (8 hours per day).
Characters who require more or less sleep will recover Power Points proportionally faster
or slower but only to the limit of a full night. For example, a character who only
requires 4 hours of sleep per night will recover 10% per hour but only up to the limit of
4 hours. The rate of recovery may vary according to the campaign’s Power Level (Section
12.1).
A fully rested caster has considerable power available, but if they expend that power
completely it will take more than a night before they have recovered.

system.name: Grace
system.description: Reduces penalties for casting spells of a higher level than the caster.

system.name: Jumping
system.description:
Jumping includes both running and standing jumps. Every character has a base jump distance depending on the type of jump. Stride is the character’s stride modifier, expressed in inches (e.g., halflings use a stride modifier of -5").

  • Running long base jump = 50" + stride
  • Standing long base jump = (50" + stride) / 2
  • Running high base jump = (50" + stride) / 5
  • Standing high base jump = (50" + stride) / 10

The difficulty modifier to jump a specific distance is +40, minus -20 for each full increment of the character’s applicable base jump distance.

If the maneuver fails, but how far the character actually did jump is important, then consult the Percentage Maneuver table to determine the distance jumped.

Example: Arkose, a goblin (with a stride modifier of -6), has a running long base jump of 44". He has a bonus of +40 jumping up to 44", +20 up to 88", +0 up to 132", -20 up to 176", etc.

system.name: Racial Lore
system.description:
Racial Lore includes recognition, knowledge of habitat and diet as well as any powers and
abilities of a specific type of race. Higher ranks will cover knowledge of any cultures,
psychology, and other details.

system.name: Trade
system.description:
This skill includes vocations that are more focused on a specific set of trade related
skills. Business and trade is an important part of many vocations, including finding
customers and suppliers as well as presenting ones goods in the best light. In other
cases, the vocation may represent work as part of a group or unit, and the skill
represents understanding how the group is coordinated and how to give and receive orders
and instructions. Many trades require other skills and these may often be applicable as
Complementary skills, e.g., a Farmer may use Survival to predict the best weather for
sowing and harvesting, or a craftsman will typically require a specific craft skill in
addition to this skill to represent their business knowledge. In other cases different
skills are needed for different aspects of the occupation, e.g., the Thief vocation may
assist in identifying marks and targets as well as selling purloined goods, but without
Stalking and Locks (or at least a little talent with a cudgel) the knowledge will be of
little use.

system.name: Flying
system.description:
As with other Movement skills, the speed of flight depends on a base movement rate
(usually defined according to the means of flight) and a selected pace. However, while
flying, a Sprint is “Diving” pace, a speed achievable only by rapidly descending, and Dash
is “Power Diving” pace, a speed achievable only by flying as hard as possible while
rapidly descending.
Flying creatures can glide at up to a running pace at half the normal movement penalties.
Unless the conditions are ideal, in the form of strong thermals or updrafts, every round
of continued gliding will require a successful maneuver at a cumulative -10 per round.

system.name: Creature Lore
system.description:
Creature Lore includes recognition, knowledge of habitat and diet as well as any powers
and abilities of a specific type of creature. Higher ranks will cover knowledge of any
cultures, psychology, and other details.
Note that lore regarding normal animals is covered by Survival for an appropriate biome.
Creature Lore is appropriate for magical creatures that do not organize themselves into
cities or tribes (for those that do, Racial Lore may be more appropriate).

system.name: Mechanics
system.description:
This skill relates to the operation or repair and construction of technology. In most
fantasy environments, mechanics will be a singular skill covering all possible mechanical
and hydraulic (pumps) devices.
At higher tech levels, this skill should become more and more specialized.
Operation covers the proper use of technological constructs, getting the maximum possible
results out of them, and avoiding overstressing them to the point of breakage. Mechanics
can be used to operate parts of a vehicle as long as it is not in motion, but in motion
the vehicle will require the Piloting skill.
Repair and Construction allows a character to assemble technological constructs from parts
or to identify jams or replace damaged parts. Construction or repair of broken parts
requires an appropriate crafting skill, and crafting new, original devices requires the
Engineering (Science category) skill.

system.name: Unarmed
system.description:
Unarmed and natural melee attacks (e.g. martial arts, bites). The stat used depends
on the specific melee attack (Section 7.1).

system.name: Transcendence
system.description: Reduces the spell-casting penalties associated with armor.

system.name: Adrenal Focus
system.description:
Adrenal Focus can be used to achieve feats of superhuman effort through concentration and
self-discipline.
With a successful maneuver the character gets a +25 bonus to any Brawn, Gymnastic, or
Movement maneuvers (+50 on an Absolute Success).

system.name: Blind Fighting
system.description: Reduces penalties to maneuvers while blind (or in darkness) or in low light (Section 15.7).

system.name: Mounted Combat
system.description: Reduces penalties to maneuvers while riding an animal or beast (Section 9.7).

system.name: Spell Lore
system.description:
Spell Lore allows a character to recognize spells that have been cast against him, or
written spells (recognition only, it cannot be used in place of Runes).
This may also provide information on expected duration or area of effect for active
spells.

system.name: Piloting
system.description:
Piloting is the operation of a vehicle such as a wagon, cart, sleigh, blimp, etc. For
animal drawn vehicles, the driver should also have Animal Handling to be able to control
the animal. Driving involves an understanding of the controls, braking, and performance
across various terrain, etc.
The Piloting maneuver may be modified by the speed of the vehicle, the angle of a turn (if
any), and the approximate size and maneuverability of the vehicle as shown in Table 3-11.
Animal powered vehicles are, in general, not particularly maneuverable, and the GM
assigned difficulty should reflect as much. For example, it is not possible to make right
angle turns with such a vehicle. When the horses turn, the rear of the cart continues
moving straight ahead until it is pulled into the curve.

system.name: Stalking
system.description:
Stalking is the ability to move in silence and unseen, using camouflage and shadows to
conceal your presence. The difficulty of the maneuver using this skill is determined
mainly by the surroundings. It will be easier in a dark, shadowy area with a lot of cover,
but more difficult in brightly lit areas without cover.
Similarly, moving across a smooth surface with lots of ambient noise makes it easier to
not be heard. Stalking is opposed by Perception skill.

system.name: Mental Focus
system.description:
Mental Focus is used to maintain concentration for extended periods of time (Section 5.5),
while stunned, or when concentrating on two things at once (Section 8.1). A GM may also
require a Mental Focus roll in extremely stressful, chaotic, or confusing situations.

system.name: Perception
system.description:
Perception is used for noticing details about the environment, and affects how well one
interprets the information. It is used to find hidden objects, to notice imperfections in
walls that may hide a secret door, to notice triggers for traps, and to sense potential
ambushes.
Perception includes all the senses, although if a particular sense is required there may
be a modifier due to a character’s superior (or inferior) sense.
If a character states that he is watching or examining an area, situation, or place, the
GM should make an Absolute Maneuver roll using the character’s Perception skill to
determine if the character notices or detects anything. The GM may keep this roll secret,
revealing only what the character has observed. A heavy penalty should be assessed (if a
roll is allowed at all) in situations where the players do not know what their characters
are looking for or do not specify that their characters are looking for something in
particular (likewise, looking for ceiling traps makes it difficult to see pit traps,
etc.).
Perception is often used as a conflicting skill against other skills like Stalking.

system.name: Animal Handling
system.description:
Animal Handling involves the care and feeding of animals, as well as training, minor
healing, and possibly simple communication depending on the type of animal. This can
include calming down agitated animals, or working them up, herding sheep or guiding a
horse, but can be as complicated as teaching the intricate tricks of a circus dog act.

system.name: Engineering
system.description:
Engineering combines aspects of mathematics, physics and invention. It provides a theoretical knowledge of devices and processes, and an understanding of why things work. Characters may use Engineering to determine what a device does, design new devices or streamline systems.

In more advanced cultures the GM may require the skill be specialized, however in a fantasy setting this is not needed (essentially this is basic mechanical and hydraulic engineering).

Use the General specialization for most fantasy settings.

system.name: Mathematics
system.description:
In the simplest form, mathematics involves counting and the basic operations of addition,
subtraction, multiplication and division. At higher levels of difficulty, it can be used
to measure and account for more and more facets of tangible things. Higher levels of
difficulty allow for more complicated manipulations, and the manipulation of more abstract
qualities and quantities. The application of many other sciences will depend on adequate
mathematical skill to carry out the necessary calculations.

system.name: Ranged Weapons
system.description:
Muscle powered thrown weapons as well as mechanical devices that fire low velocity projectiles.
Skill bonus is based on developed specialization.

system.name: Social Awareness
system.description:
This skill develops awareness of the motives and social maneuvers of those around you. You
can make maneuvers using this skill to study other people and try to understand them,
determine if they are lying, or otherwise infer their motives. If someone is using this
skill (i.e., not relaxed with his guard down) when targeted with an Influence skill
maneuver (see above) then he can make a conflicting maneuver to notice the Influence
attempt.

system.name: Weight Training
system.description:
Weight Training aids in using one’s muscles to the most advantage with the least chance of
becoming injured. This covers the proper ways to get a solid grip on objects, the right
way to apply strength to lift or move something, and the correct ways to position your
body when moving to keep applying force without hurting yourself. This skill is used as
the bonus for strength-based feats (Section 5.2).

system.name: Closed
system.description:
Developing a spell list gives a character the ability to cast spells from that list. The number of ranks a character has in a list determines the level to which he can cast from that list (e.g., if a character has 8 ranks in Fire Law he can cast any spell from the Fire Law list up to 8th level). The number of ranks in the spell list plus the caster’s realm stat bonus (once) is also added to the Spellcasting Roll when a spell is cast. The full skill bonus in a Spell List is used for Spell Mastery: attempts to change the spell when it is cast (e.g., making a Fire Ball diameter smaller or shaping a Wall of Fire). Other uses are occasionally specified in certain spells.

There are 5 different Spell List skills: Base, Open, Closed, Arcane, and Restricted, with each individual spell list as specializations. Base lists are the specialized spell lists of each magic-using profession. Open lists are common, relatively straightforward spells that may be understood by anyone using the realm. Closed lists represent more esoteric magical techniques which may be understood by any user of the realm, but with greater difficulty. Arcane lists are more obscure or exotic magics which exist outside of the three realms. Restricted lists include any list the GM allows you to learn which is not a Base, Open, Closed, or Arcane list (e.g., the Base list of another profession). You may not develop ranks in lists from realms other than your own.

Each Base, Open, Closed, Arcane, or Restricted Spell List requires separate skill specialization

system.name: Herbalism
system.description:
Herbalism includes knowledge of effects and doses, preparation, and application of herbs
and medicines.
Searching for herbs should use Survival skill for the appropriate biome, although
Herbalism may be used as a Complementary skill. Detailed rules on herbs appear in Treasure
Law. In higher tech societies, this skill could be replaced with Pharmacology.

system.name: Solar Recovery
system.description: Ky-taari are invigorated by sunlight, but less energetic without it. When a Kytaari is in sunlight, they recover from fatigue penalties at double the normal rate (reducing penalties by 2 for every minute of rest). However, when there is no sunlight at all (e.g., underground or at night), they recover from fatigue at half the normal rate (reducing penalties by 1 for every 2 minutes of rest).

system.name: Traction (Synshari)
system.description: Synshari move as easily on sand or similar loose material as they do on solid ground. However, they do not have any advantage on snow, ice, or mud, or on wet or oily surfaces.

system.name: Opportunistic Strike
system.description:
You have learned to take advantage of your foe's misfortunes with one melee
Combat Training specialization. If in melee combat with a foe, and your foe
fumbles, you may make an immediate attack roll against him (in addition to any
normal attack that round). This attack does not require any AP and your OB is
not reduced for the number of AP used or for Parrying.

system.name: Phobia
system.description: You have an irrational and uncontrollable fear of something. Whenever you encounter it, you must make a RR vs fear, taking the effects as shown in Core Law on Table 14-3a. If surrender is not appropriate for the subject of your fear (e.g., you are afraid of heights, or it is a creature in the far-off distance), any surrender result indicates paralysis for one round per 10 failure. If you are seeing the source of your fear at a safe distance, treat it as a 3rd level fear attack. If you must interact with it directly, treat it as 10th level. If you will be surrounded by it, treat it as 20th level. If you will be in combat against it, add its level to these values. At Tier I, the subject of your fear is something uncommon, such as the number 13, mechanical devices in a medieval setting, or dragons. At Tier II, you fear something moderately common, such as heights, enclosed spaces, crowds, or orcs. At Tier III, it will be encountered very commonly, such as water, blood, or bladed objects.

system.name: Deadeye
system.description:
You have uncanny aim with a ranged weapon. All range penalties for a ranged
Combat Training specialization may be reduced by up to 10/Tier.

system.name: Temporal Skills
system.description:
Spells from one of your spell lists last longer than normal and have their
duration increased by +50%/Tier. This only affects spells that have a duration.

system.name: Hearing, Dog
system.description:
You have hearing as sensitive as a dog. Dogs can pinpoint nearby sounds with
high accuracy and may hear sounds up to 4 times as far away as a human,
including very high-pitched sounds. This grants +10 on sound-based Perception
maneuvers.

system.name: Beast of Burden
system.description:
Your body is particularly well-suited for carrying heavy loads. You may carry an
additional 10%/Tier of your body weight as encumbrance without penalty, except
that encumbrance penalties are not reduced for purposes of Dodging.

system.name: Multilingual
system.description:
You grew up in a multilingual culture or have always been able to learn
languages quickly when you immerse yourself in them. You gain 10 ranks in one
language or 5 ranks in each of two languages.

system.name: Acute Vision
system.description:
You have heightened sight, providing +5/Tier to Perception rolls involving
vision.

system.name: Light Sensitivity
system.description:
You cannot take direct sunlight, and you are at a penalty of -25/Tier when in
bright light equal to direct sunlight. (This penalty is reduced by 25 in light
equal to a cloudy day, by 50 for partially shaded or cloudy conditions, and by
75 in full shadows such as under storm clouds or heavy tree cover).

system.name: Missing Sense (Feel/Touch)
system.description:
You are completely missing a sense. You suffer a -100 penalty on
actions requiring the sense (if it is possible at all) and from -20 to -50 on
actions which would benefit from the sense.

system.name: Fragile
system.description:
You are exceptionally fragile and have a lower pain tolerance than others. This
grants a -5/Tier modifier to base hits. Base hits are normally equal to 25.

system.name: Direction Sense
system.description:
By detecting the planet's magnetic field or other means, you are always able to
discern which direction is north. This grants a +30 bonus to Navigation.

system.name: Natural Armor
system.description:
Your skin (hide, carapace, etc.) is resistant to attacks as if you were wearing
armor and gives +1 AT / Tier (AT 1 is no armor). This natural armor moves
naturally with you and incurs no encumbrance or maneuver penalties. It also does
not interfere with magic, so it provides no RR bonus against spells, nor does it
hinder your own casting. If combined with worn armor, use the higher AT (do not
add them together), and if the worn armor is heavier add the number of tiers as
DB.

system.name: Slow Healer
system.description: You recover slower than normal. Recovery times are doubled.

system.name: Inferior Stat
system.description:
An average being of your race is inferior in one of the 10 statistics over the
average human. You get -1/Tier to the stats bonus. This talent can only be taken
as a racial talent.

system.name: Tough
system.description:
You are exceptionally tough and have a higher pain tolerance than others. This
grants a +5/Tier modifier to base hits. Base hits are normally equal to 25.

system.name: Physical Resistance
system.description:
You have an innate resistance to physical ailments (e.g., poison, disease) and
receive +5/Tier to all Physical Resistance Rolls.

system.name: Prehensile Appendage
system.description: The creature has a tail, trunk, or other appendage which is dexterous enough to hold and grasp objects.

system.name: Acute Hearing
system.description:
You have a heightened sense of hearing, providing +5/Tier to Perception rolls
involving hearing.

system.name: Lesser Nightvision
system.description: Although you don’t have the full Nightvision ability that some races are blessed with, your eyes adapt quickly to darkness and you can get around reasonably well at night. All penalties for darkness (other than pitch dark conditions) are reduced by 20. This reduction is not cumulative with any spell, effect, or ability which grants Nightvision.

system.name: Magical Resistance
system.description:
You have an innate resistance to one of the realms of magic and receive +5/Tier
to all Resistance Rolls versus that realm.

system.name: Increased Size
system.description:
You are one size (per Tier) larger than medium. Larger size makes your attacks
more powerful and increases your number of concussion hits (Section 9.4).

system.name: Decreased Size
system.description:
You are one size (per Tier) smaller than medium. Smaller size weakens your
attacks and reduces your concussion hits (Section 9.4).

system.name: Hearing, Hare
system.description:
Your range of hearing is very good in the high and low frequency range. You may
also localize sounds with great accuracy and hear danger coming from 10 times
farther than a human. You gain +20 on hearing Perception maneuvers.

system.name: Acute Smell
system.description:
You have a heightened sense of smell, providing +5/Tier to Perception rolls
involving smell.

system.name: Inept
system.description:
You are inexplicably jinxed and suffer -5/Tier to all maneuvers in a single
skill (all specializations).

system.name: Prodigy
system.description:
You have some unusual innate ability or supernatural aid that gives a bonus of
+5/Tier to a single skill (all specializations).

system.name: Cold Resistant
system.description: You are highly tolerant of cold conditions. You suffer no effects of cold temperatures down to 30°F (-1°C), and Endurance penalties apply only for every 5°F below that limit. For other effects of natural cold, you suffer effects as if the temperature was 30°F higher. This talent does not protect you against cold-based attacks and spells. At Tier II, you suffer no effects down to 10°F (-12°C) and otherwise treat effects as if the temperature was 50°F higher. The second Tier is normally appropriate only as a racial talent.

system.name: Hibernation (Nomari)
system.description: The Nomari can put themselves into a state of deep hibernation, during which they require no food or water and only minimal air. It is difficult to rouse them from this condition and they will suffer activity penalties while they are gradually waking up, as well as being extremely hungry and thirsty.

system.name: Camouflage, Pattern
system.description: The creature's hide is well suited to concealment in one particular type of terrain (e.g., forest, desert). While in this terrain, it gains a +25 bonus to Stalking.

system.name: Missing Sense (Sight)
system.description:
You are completely missing a sense. You suffer a -100 penalty on actions
requiring the sense (if it is possible at all) and from -20 to -50 on actions
which would benefit from the sense (e.g. -50 might appropriate for many maneuvers
for blind characters).

system.name: Golden Throat
system.description:
You have a soothing and calming voice. This gives +10/Tier to any maneuver to
verbally calm or persuade (Charm, Singing, Leadership, etc.).

system.name: Lesser Attack
system.description:
Your attack (e.g., Bite, Striking) is weak relative to your size and is
decreased by -1 size/Tier.

system.name: Heat Resistant
system.description: You are highly tolerant of hot conditions. You suffer no effects of hot temperatures up to 110°F (43°C), and Endurance penalties apply only for every 5°F below that limit. You resist sunburn and you require only normal water rations even in hot conditions. This talent does not protect you against heat-based attacks and spells. At Tier II, you suffer no effects up to 130°F (54°C). The second Tier is normally appropriate only as a racial talent.

system.name: Defensive Aura
system.description:
A glowing or blurred aura surrounds you, making you more difficult to target.
You receive +5 DB/Tier, which is not cumulative with any Aura or Blur spell.

system.name: Visions
system.description:
You are able to receive spontaneous visions of persons/places/objects based upon
objects that you touch with your bare skin. The details of the vision are at the
discretion of the GM, but should reveal details of a significant event relating
to the object, if any. (That a knife was touched by a rat two days ago is
usually an insignificant event, that it was used to murder someone a week ago is
usually very significant). This can be used one time per day for every Tier.

system.name: Sight, Eagle
system.description:
Your keen eyesight permits both good peripheral vision as well as the ability to
focus on distant objects, such as a hare two miles away. You gain a +20 bonus to
all vision-based Perception maneuvers.

system.name: Disturbing Voice
system.description:
The character has a grating or annoying tone of voice. This gives a penalty of
-20/Tier to any maneuver to verbally calm or persuade (Influence skills,
Performance Art: Singing, Leadership, etc.)

system.name: Fast Healer
system.description: You recover faster than normal. Recovery times are cut in half.

system.name: Math Illiterate
system.description:
You never learned basic math and have a very hard time with numbers. You cannot
add or subtract without your fingers, cannot multiply at all, and cannot count
higher than 20.

system.name: Climbing, Claw
system.description: The creature's claws can be used to climb on soft or rough surfaces. It cannot hold on for long, but climbing short stints is easy. Climbing claws are ideal for climbing trees, slippery and oily surfaces, and any fairly soft material. On such surfaces, the creature has a BMR of 16'/round at up to a Jog (2x) pace. On natural rock surfaces, a climbing roll is needed at +10.

system.name: Slow on the Draw
system.description:
You are clumsy with all weapons when surprised. Drawing your weapon or readying
an arrow takes you 2 AP.

system.name: Immune to Disease
system.description:
You are of exceptional health, or of a nature that is not subject to disease.
You are immune to all normal, natural diseases (Tier I) or all diseases
including magical ones (Tier II).

system.name: Strike Reflex
system.description:
Your powerful strike reflex allows you to act with tremendous speed, gaining a
+20 initiative modifier, when the reflex is triggered by any sudden movement
towards or away from you by a target within range of your attack. This
instinctive response is impossible for you to quell, even if you want to; you
must take immediate offensive action in the round in which you are startled,
rather than waiting to see what is happening.

system.name: Spatial Skills
system.description:
Spells from one of your spell lists work at greater distances than normal and
have their ranges increased by +50%/Tier.

system.name: One Eye
system.description:
You have sight only in one eye. The other may be missing, replaced with a glass
eye, or covered with an eyepatch. You lack distance perception and peripheral
vision on the affected side, and all ranged attacks suffer a -25 penalty.

system.name: Destiny Sense
system.description:
You instinctively know the direction (Tier I) or direction and distance (Tier
II) that will take you to a specific goal. This can be used once per day.

system.name: Darkvision
system.description:
You can see 10'/Tier feet even in complete darkness. (Usually you must also have
the Nightvision talent, but the GM may choose to allow it to be taken alone for
some setting-specific reason.) The second tier and above costs only 5 instead of
10.

system.name: Missing Sense (Smell)
system.description:
You are completely missing a sense. You suffer a -100 penalty on actions
requiring the sense (if it is possible at all) and from -20 to -50 on actions
which would benefit from the sense (e.g. -20 might be appropriate for a deaf
character on a Perception check to avoid being ambushed, while -50 is
appropriate for many maneuvers for blind characters).

system.name: Empathy
system.description:
You can read emotions of those within 25'. If a target is trying to hide his
emotions, he gets a Resistance Roll vs. your level; Success means that you
cannot read that target for 24 hours. This ability grants a +50 bonus to
Social Awareness when appropriate.

system.name: Rapid Bleeder
system.description:
Your body has an abnormal inability to clot bleeding wounds. Each bleeding
injury is increased by 1 hit/round for each Tier. The injury is modified at the
moment it is inflicted; it does not open an additional 1 point of bleeding each
round.

system.name: Missing Sense (Hearing)
system.description:
You are completely missing a sense. You suffer a -100 penalty on
actions requiring the sense (if it is possible at all) and from -20 to -50 on
actions which would benefit from the sense (e.g. -20 might be appropriate for
a deaf character on a Perception check to avoid being ambushed). 
Deaf characters (and others) may develop lip-reading for a given language
as a Language specialization.

system.name: Perfect Pitch
system.description:
You have perfect pitch and are able to reproduce any pitch with either your
voice (if possible with your vocal cords) or an appropriate instrument. This
allows you to play most pieces of music after hearing them. You get +10/Tier to
any Performance Art: Singing or Play Instrument skill. This cannot be combined
with Golden Throat to get a higher bonus to Singing. Use the talent with the
highest bonus.

system.name: Increased Stride
system.description: Your base movement rate is increased by 2'/round for each tier.

system.name: Amphibious
system.description: Although capable of surviving out of water, the creature requires immersion in water at regular intervals. It may stay dry for up to one day before returning to the water. After this time, it suffers a penalty of -1 per hour it has spent out of the water. This penalty may only be removed by immersion in water.

system.name: Animal Empathy
system.description:
You have an affinity with a particular kind of animal. Any maneuvers involving
one type of animal (dogs, cats, marine mammals, fish, hooved mammals, etc.) are
at +25. In addition, if you associate with an animal of that type for one month,
you and the animal will be able to communicate empathically to a range of 100'.
For each Tier beyond Tier I, the range is increased by 25'.

system.name: Sight, Hawk
system.description:
Your vision is exceptional, permitting you to see objects up to 5 miles away
with great sharpness, with good depth perception and the ability to spot tiny
movements. You gain a +30 bonus to all vision-based Perception maneuvers.

system.name: Trogli Joints
system.description: Trogli gain a bonus of +10 on contortions, balance, throwing, and fine manual work such as picking locks.

system.name: Ambidextrous
system.description:
You are able to use either hand equally well for all maneuvers and activities.
The normal -20 penalty for off-hand usage does not apply.

system.name: Distinct Odor
system.description:
The character with this flaw has a distinct odor, which will transfer to objects
the character touches with bare skin. This grants a +50 bonus to Perception and
Tracking efforts based on smell. (If the odor is foul or unpleasant enough to
harm social interactions, the character should also take the Inept flaw for
Influence skills).

system.name: Additional Limb Pair
system.description:
You possess an additional pair of arms per Tier. The additional arms may be used
to manipulate and to make attacks (with the usual penalties for multiple
attacks). If the additional limbs are legs and unable to make attacks, use
Increased Stride rather than this talent.

system.name: Heat Intolerant
system.description: Although Lydians handle cold easily, they are uncomfortable in warmer conditions. They cannot acclimate to temperatures above 80°F (27.5°C) and suffer -5 Endurance penalties for each 5°F above this temperature.

system.name: Sharpshooter
system.description:
You have learned the importance of patience when using your ranged weapon. For
each full round you spend aiming, you gain +5 to your OB with one ranged Combat
Training specialization, to a maximum of +5/Tier.

system.name: Walking, Quadrupedal
system.description:
As quadrupeds, Centaurs have a base movement rate (BMR) of 30’/round, with a maximum pace of Dash, and gain a +10 bonus to their Running skill.

(Note that Centaurs also have a +5 stride bonus, so their actual BMR before modification for their Quickness bonus is 35’/round.)

system.name: Neutral Odor
system.description:
You naturally have a very weak odor. This makes all attempts to perceive your
presence based upon the sense of smell operate at -50. This penalty may be
reduced if you are carrying any objects or equipment that carry strong odors
(e.g., garlic, rotting fish).

system.name: Mumbler
system.description: You get a penalty of -5/Tier to all Spellcasting rolls.

system.name: Albino
system.description: You are highly tolerant of cold conditions. You suffer no effects of cold temperatures down to 30°F (-1°C), and Endurance penalties apply only for every 5°F below that limit. For other effects of natural cold, you suffer effects as if the temperature was 30°F higher. This talent does not protect you against cold-based attacks and spells. At Tier II, you suffer no effects down to 10°F (-12°C) and otherwise treat effects as if the temperature was 50°F higher. The second Tier is normally appropriate only as a racial talent.

system.name: Natural Weaponry
system.description:
You have some type of natural weaponry (e.g., a Bite, Claw, Sting, Horn, etc.)
and may develop skill with it and make attacks equal to your size. Use the
Enhanced Attack or Lesser Attack talent to increase or decrease its size. This
allows creatures to get an attack at -1 size for free, although one cannot
receive points for taking natural weaponry at less than -1 size.

system.name: None
system.description:
Humans are the standard against which all other races are compared.
However, humans do benefit from a high number of bonus DP (as shown
on Table 2-2a). Even the more powerful High men, despite their stature,
are essentially human.

system.name: Quickdraw
system.description:
You have mastered drawing a weapon quickly. Drawing a specified Melee Combat
Training specialization is treated as instantaneous (0 AP) rather than 1 AP.

system.name: Disturbing Form
system.description: Other races find your appearance to be extremely disturbing. This gives a penalty of -20 to any maneuver to calm or persuade, if you are visible.

system.name: Superior Stat
system.description:
An average being of your race is superior in one of the 10 statistics over the
average human. You get +1/Tier to the stats bonus. This talent can only be taken
as a racial talent.

system.name: Air and Water Breathing
system.description: The creature can breathe water as easily as air, allowing it to survive easily both in and out of water. (For creatures that breathe water but not air, use the Gills talent instead.)

system.name: Mute
system.description:
You cannot speak, although you can understand speech and may communicate via
other means such as sign language or gesture if you have the ability to do so.

system.name: Sense Weakness
system.description:
You are able to sense a foe's weakness by making a Perception roll
(Concentration action for one round) while observing the foe for 1 round. With a
Success, you may reroll one critical against him (the second roll stands). You
may decide after your initial critical roll whether to use your reroll or save
it for a later attack. You may sense the weakness of the same foe again after
you have used your reroll. If you sense the weakness of a different foe before
using your reroll, the first reroll is lost.

system.name: Poor Smell
system.description:
You have a deficient sense of smell, providing -5/Tier to Perception rolls
involving smell.

system.name: Quick-Caster
system.description:
You are particularly adept at quickly casting spells from one of your spell
lists. The number of Action Points (normally 2-4 AP) required to cast a spell
from the list is 2-3 AP (Tier I) or 2 AP (Tier II).

system.name: Tetrachromatic Vision
system.description:
Your vision encompasses normal color vision as well as sensitivity to
ultraviolet light. Your sense of colors differs from other races, and you are
also more sensitive to cues others cannot see. Penalties for spotting invisible
(including hidden by the Unseen spell) and camouflaged people and objects are
reduced by 30.

system.name: Camouflage (Kuluku)
system.description: By concentrating, Kuluku can change their coloration to better match their environment, gaining a +50 bonus to Stalking. When they stop concentrating, the effect will continue for one round per level.

system.name: Magical Vulnerability
system.description:
You have an innate vulnerability to one of the realms of magic and receive
-5/Tier to all Resistance Rolls versus that realm.

system.name: Poor Hearing
system.description:
You have a deficient sense of hearing, providing -5/Tier to Perception rolls
involving hearing.

system.name: Elemental Resistance
system.description:
You are particularly resistant to one of: Cold/Ice, Heat/Fire, or
Electricity/Light. You gain a +5/Tier bonus to DBs, RRs, and Endurance against
the selected element. If the effect is a fixed critical and none of these
bonuses apply, the critical is reduced by one severity for every 2 Tiers.
Modifiers also apply to extreme environmental conditions (e.g. Resistance to
Heat/Fire would give an Endurance bonus when traveling in an extremely hot
desert).

system.name: Poor Vision
system.description:
You have deficient sight, providing -5/Tier to Perception rolls involving
vision.

system.name: Uncoordinated
system.description:
You are terribly uncoordinated and have a difficult time moving and performing
other actions. Penalties to actions made while moving are treated as if you were
moving 1 pace (Tier I) or 2 paces (Tier II) higher than your actual pace.

system.name: Pressing the Advantage
system.description:
You have an aggressive fighting style using one melee Combat Training specializations.
Every time you inflict a critical on your opponent you get a +10 OB/Tier to your next
attack against this foe.

system.name: Non-violent
system.description:
You do not want to hurt others, and flinch with remorse when doing so. After
inflicting a critical, any action you take in the following round suffers a
penalty of -20/Tier.

system.name: Photosynthetic Skin
system.description: Although this unique trait is not sufficient to replace food, it does explain their considerable endurance (this is not considered a separate talent, aside from their Endurance bonus).

system.name: Frenzy
system.description:
You can enter a frenzied rage with a successful Adrenal Focus maneuver. While
frenzied, you gain a +5 Strength bonus, your attacks are treated as +1 Size, and
you suffer no penalties due to hit loss. Instead of falling unconscious at 0
Hits, you will continue to fight until you reach negative hits equal to your
Body Development skill, at which point you will fall unconscious. Once
unconscious you must make a Physical RR each round until you either fail (and
die) or are healed enough hits to be above this threshold. While frenzied, you
get no Defensive Bonus other than that due to magic and are unable to allocate
OB to parry attacks. Furthermore, you will always attack the closest creature
(medium Perception roll required to distinguish friend from foe) and an Adrenal
Focus maneuver is required to exit the frenzied rage. If there are no animate
targets left to attack, you will destroy anything else within reach until
knocked unconscious or you make a successful maneuver to come out of frenzy.

system.name: Sight, Gecko
system.description:
Your eyes perform like those of a gecko, permitting additional detail close-up
as well as good depth vision and you do not lose your color vision in dark
conditions (normal penalties for darkness still apply). You gain a +10 bonus to
all vision-based Perception maneuvers.

system.name: Eloquence
system.description:
You are exceptionally gifted at magic and receive +5/Tier to all Spellcasting
rolls.

system.name: Decreased Stride
system.description: Your base movement rate is decreased by 2'/round for each tier.

system.name: Missing Sense (Taste)
system.description:
You are completely missing a sense. You suffer a -100 penalty on actions
requiring the sense (if it is possible at all) and from -20 to -50 on actions
which would benefit from the sense.

system.name: Physical Vulnerability
system.description:
You have an innate vulnerability to physical ailments (e.g., poison, disease)
and receive -5/Tier to all Physical Resistance Rolls.

system.name: Heatsense
system.description:
You have a very sensitive tongue, antennae, or sensor pits that allow you to
gauge temperature at close range up to 1/1000th of a degree. You may use this to
sense prey nearby, or detect tracks of prey within several hours of its passing.
This grants a bonus up to +20 on Perception and Tracking maneuvers to detect
living creatures or other warm or cold objects, as long as you come within close
proximity to them or their tracks.

system.name: Restricted Diet
system.description:
Your diet is limited to certain foods which are normally available but may not
be in all circumstances. Other foods either provide no sustenance or will cause
you to operate at significant penalties (whether due to upset stomach or
wracking guilt) of at least -20 for the next 24 hours. Examples include a
completely vegetarian diet or a carnivore diet which depends entirely on meat. A
restricted diet may increase the cost of your provisions or decrease the chance
of finding suitable fare.

system.name: Innate Spell List
system.description: The creature is endowed with the knowledge or special abilities permitting it to use a single selected spell list to spells up to a level equal to the Tier. Spells are cast as described in Spell Law section 4.8, including a spell casting roll and chance of spell failure. Innate spell-lists are treated as Base lists for SCR.

system.name: Heavy Sleeper
system.description:
You are difficult to awaken and receive a -25 to Perception rolls to awaken. The
difficulty of the maneuver is set by the GM depending on the conditions.

system.name: Elemental Susceptibility
system.description:
You are particularly susceptible to one of: Cold/Ice, Heat/Fire, or
Electricity/Light. You suffer a -5/Tier penalty to DBs, RRs, and Endurance
against the selected element. If the effect is a fixed critical and none of
these bonuses apply, the critical is increased by one severity for every 2
Tiers. Modifiers also apply to extreme environmental conditions (e.g.
Susceptibility to Heat/Fire would give an Endurance penalty when traveling in an
extremely hot desert).

system.name: Light-boned
system.description:
You are lightly built and relatively fragile for your size. Your concussion hits
and any attacks made against you are adjusted as if you were one size smaller
per Tier. Attacks you make against others are not adjusted.

system.name: Poor Taste
system.description:
You suffer from a deficient sense of taste, providing -5/Tier to Perception
rolls involving taste.

system.name: Fast Attack
system.description:
Your quick reflexes permit you to act before others. You gain +5/Tier to your
Initiative.

system.name: Efficient Sleeper
system.description:
You require less sleep than most people, able to get benefits from 3 hours (Tier
I) or 2 hours (Tier II) of sleep as others do in 4. Both Efficient Sleeper and
Restless Sleeper will change the rate at which you recover Power Points, but not
the total you recover per night of sleep. For example, Tier II of Efficient
Sleeper allows you to recover twice as many Power Points per hour but you will
not recover more by sleeping more than your required 4 hours of sleep per night.

system.name: Cold Sensitive
system.description: You suffer a penalty of -1 /Tier per degree below 40°F on all actions.

system.name: Acute Touch
system.description:
You have unusually sensitive tactile senses, providing +5/Tier to Perception
rolls involving touch.

system.name: Restless Sleeper
system.description:
You toss and turn and have a hard time getting restful sleep and thus must sleep
5 hours (Tier I) or 6 hours (Tier II) to get the benefit of 4 hours. Both
Efficient Sleeper and Restless Sleeper will change the rate at which you recover
Power Points, but not the total you recover per night of sleep. For example,
Tier II of Efficient Sleeper allows you to recover twice as many Power Points
per hour but you will not recover more by sleeping more than your required 4
hours of sleep per night.

system.name: Acute Taste
system.description:
You enjoy a superb sense of taste, providing +5/Tier to Perception rolls
involving taste.

system.name: Inglorious Failure
system.description: When you suffer a Spell Failure, your Spell Failure roll is increased by 5/Tier.

system.name: Graceful Recovery
system.description:
You have a lower chance of catastrophic failure when casting spells. Spell
Failure rolls are reduced by up to 5/Tier (to a minimum of 1).

system.name: Poor Touch
system.description:
You have unusually deficient tactile senses, providing -5/Tier to Perception
rolls involving touch.

system.name: Foiler
system.description:
You have incorporated moves in one melee Combat Training specialization designed
to cause your opponent to mishandle his weapon. Any round you use this talent,
any foe attacking you that you are aware of has the fumble numbers of all his
weapons increased by 1/Tier.

system.name: Vigorous
system.description: You have incredible stamina. You get a +10/Tier modifier to all Endurance rolls.

system.name: Breath Holding
system.description:
You may hold your breath for up to 1 minute per character level. If you remain
inactive, the time may be doubled, or tripled with a successful Meditation
maneuver.

system.name: Quickload
system.description:
You have mastered loading a missile weapon quickly. Loading for a specified ranged Combat
Training specialization is treated as instantaneous (0 AP) rather than 1 AP.

system.name: Wings, Vestigial
system.description:
You have small wings which are not adequate for flight, but which do provide a
+10 bonus to Jumping and when using Acrobatics to reduce the impact of a fall.

system.name: Iron Will
system.description:
You have formidable willpower, and get a bonus of +5/Tier to Resistance Rolls
versus mental spells (attack, informational, or otherwise).

system.name: Scope Skills
system.description:
Spells from one of your spell lists affect a greater area than normal and have
their radius or # of targets increased by +100%/Tier. If used with directed
spells (e.g. Bolts), your applicable directed spells OB must be split between
the attacks.

system.name: Wings, Flying
system.description:
The creature is capable of winged flight (See Table 4-1f). Paces above Run (at Tier III+) may only be achieved while diving (Sprint) or power diving (Dash). See RMCL section 3.17 for more details, including about gliding.

system.name: Poison Injection
system.description:
One of your natural attacks (typically a bite or stinger) injects poison. If the
attack scores a critical (any severity), the target must make a Physical RR
against your level or suffer the effect of the poison (typically Circulatory
poison).

system.name: Slow Bleeder
system.description:
Your body has an abnormal ability to clot bleeding wounds. Each bleeding injury
is reduced by 1 hit/round for each Tier. Slow Bleeder may prevent bleeding
entirely. The injury is modified at the moment it is inflicted; it does not clot
an additional 1 point of bleeding each round.

system.name: Subconscious Discipline
system.description:
You are able to extend the duration of your Concentration based spells beyond
your actual time of concentration. The spell will continue for half (Tier I) or
the total (Tier II) rounds spent concentrating after concentration has ceased.

system.name: Extended Reach
system.description:
You are able to cast Touch spells from a single spell list with a range of
5'/Tier. Any range modifiers apply normally, using the actual range.

system.name: Light Sleeper
system.description:
You receive a +25 bonus to Perception rolls to awake from sleep. The difficulty
of the maneuver is set by the GM depending on the conditions.

system.name: Nightvision
system.description:
You can see in dim light, equivalent to nighttime conditions, as well as a human
can see in daylight. All penalties for darkness (other than complete, pitch dark
conditions) are reduced by 40. However, while using Nightvision you are more
susceptible to sudden bright lights. Range is still limited by environmental
factors (e.g., haze, fog). See Section 15.7 for more details.

system.name: Recurved Musculature
system.description:
Your muscles have tremendous capacity and also store potential energy, allowing
them to work like springs. Your base jump distance (see Jumping skill in chapter
3) is tripled, and you receive a +20 bonus to Acrobatics, Climbing, Jumping, and
Running maneuvers other than Dodging.

system.name: Enhanced Attack
system.description:
You are able to put an incredible amount of momentum and power into one of your
attacks (e.g., Bite, Striking). Its size is increased by +1 size/Tier.

system.name: Revulsion
system.description:
You cannot stand the sight of blood. Each round a bleeding character (or a
bloody corpse) is in view, the character must make a Fear/Terror RR equal to the
amount of bleeding that is visible (so if the character can see two combatants,
one bleeding 3/round, and one bleeding at 2/round, the fear RR is vs. a level 5
attack). Treat bloody corpses as 10/round bleeding for this calculation.

system.name: Extra Sense
system.description:
You can sense something that normally cannot be sensed (allowing Perception
rolls). This sense must be specified when taken, and appropriately described
(e.g., able to smell fear or can feel evil magic). The GM should be wary
about how broadly a sense is described, and may narrow it.
Tier I: Sense things inside body or affecting character (i.e., like taste).
Tier II: Sense things in contact with body (i.e., like feel/touch).
Tier III: General sense of direction and intensity (i.e., like smell). Can attack
otherwise unseen targets at -50.
Tier IV: Direction, intensity, and distance, weak on specific
details (i.e., like hearing). Can attack otherwise unseen targets at -25.
Tier V: Can sense in specific detail (i.e., like sight), can attack otherwise unseen
targets normally using just this sense.

system.name: Third Eyelid
system.description:
Your eyes have a transparent additional eyelid, or nictating membrane, which
protects them while still permitting sight. You are unaffected by dust, sand, or
water which otherwise might limit use of your eyes.

system.name: Awkward Movement
system.description:
One of the creature's movement modes, such as walking, swimming, or flying, is slow and clumsy. Attacks that depend on movement, such as Trample or Ram, suffer twice the listed maneuver penalty. In addition, DB is halved. See 4-1: Awkward Movement Talent Details.

system.name: Power Recycling
system.description:
When you fail casting a spell you are able to recover half (Tier I) or all (Tier
II) of the Power Points used.

system.name: Swimming
system.description:
The creature is to some extent adapted to movement in the water, ranging from a basic ability to float and paddle (Tier I) to webbed feet (Tier II) or a streamlined form (Tier IV) or even an unnatural ability to move without resistance through the water (Tier V). system.name: Hearing, Cat
system.description:
Your hearing is equivalent to that of a cat. It is not more sensitive to most
sounds than the hearing of a human, but you are able to hear very high-pitched
sounds, such as some calls of rats and mice and those of sonar-using bats. In
addition, you have an improved ability to determine the location of a sound's
source, gaining +10 on Perception maneuvers to locate a sound.

system.name: Extra Joints
system.description:
Your limbs are multiply-jointed or extra flexible (e.g., a tentacle) and agile.
All activity with the limb, including melee, throwing, and movement, gains a +20
bonus.

system.name: Feeble
system.description:
You suffer from a lack of stamina. You get a -10/Tier modifier to all Endurance
rolls.

system.name: Riposte
system.description:
When using all of your OB to parry with one melee Combat Training
specialization, you may attempt a riposte attack. If the parry is effective (no
hits delivered), you may make an immediate (0 AP) attack with an OB of 50 minus
the foe's total modified attack roll. (e.g., an attack roll of 35 would result
in a +15 riposte attack, while an attack roll of 70 would result in a -20
riposte attack).

system.name: Look of Eagles
system.description:
With the gift of inspiration, you get +10/Tier to all Leadership maneuvers and
followers get +2/Tier to fear RRs.

system.name: Shapechange, Legs
system.description: A Merman capable of transforming their tail into legs does not suffer these penalties while they have legs; this may be purchased as an 8 DP talent, requiring 1 minute to transform and lasting for 4 hours plus 1 hour per level.
